style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The last psalm of Book One, and it ends the way the book began -- with a beatitude. Psalm 1 blessed the man who delights in the law; Psalm 41 blesses the man who pays wise attention to the weak, and promises that the LORD will be at his bedside when he is the weak one: guarding, keeping alive, propping him up, turning the whole mattress in his illness. Then David is the sick man. He asks for healing on the ground of confession, not merit -- heal my soul, for I have sinned against You -- while the visitors count down to his death, speak hollow comfort at the bedside, and go outside to talk. Worst of all, the man of his peace, who ate his bread, has lifted his heel against him: Ahithophel first, and then, at another table, Judas -- Jesus quoted the line and left out 'in whom I trusted.' The prayer is for the one verb the enemies denied him: raise me up. He gets it, reads his survival as God's delight, and finds himself stationed before God's face forever. The doxology that follows is the editors' seal on the whole first book: blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and Amen.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David. Blessed is the one who gives thought to the weak; in the day of evil the LORD will bring him through.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. Blessed [esher -- happy] is he that considers [sakal -- gives wise attention to] the poor ['the weak, or, sick', dal, the KJV margin]: the LORD [YHWH] will deliver [malat -- let slip free] him in time ['in the day of evil', yom ra, the KJV margin] of trouble.
1.notes: ashre maskil el-dal (H835, H7919, H1800): happy the one who deals WISELY with the dal -- the low, the weak, the margin's 'sick' -- sakal, the insight-verb: not a coin tossed but attention paid; be-yom raah yemalletehu YHWH (H3117, H7451, H4422, H3068): in the day of evil the LORD will let him slip free. Book One of the Psalter opens with a beatitude (1:1) and closes with this one: the blessed man of Psalm 1 turns out to be a man who notices the sick.

2.text: The LORD will guard him and keep him alive; he will be called blessed in the land -- and You will not hand him over to the appetite of his enemies.
2.amp: The LORD [YHWH] will preserve [shamar -- guard] him, and keep him alive [chayah]; and he shall be blessed [ashar -- called happy] upon the earth [eretz]: and You will not deliver ['do not thou deliver', natan, the KJV margin] him unto the will [nephesh -- appetite] of his enemies [oyeb].
2.notes: YHWH yishmerehu vi-chayyehu (H3068, H8104, H2421): the LORD will guard him and make him live -- ve-ushshar ba-aretz (H833, H776): and he will be pronounced happy in the land -- ve-al-tittenehu be-nephesh oyebav (H5414, H5315, H341): 'and do not give him', the margin's imperative, to the nephesh of his enemies -- their appetite, the throat that wants to swallow him. Blessing stated, then prayed.

3.text: The LORD will sustain him on his sickbed; You turn his whole bed over in his illness.
3.amp: The LORD [YHWH] will strengthen [saad -- sustain, prop up] him upon the bed of languishing [devay -- illness]: You will make ['turn', haphak, the KJV margin] all his bed [mishkab] in his sickness [choli].
3.notes: YHWH yisadennu al-eres devai (H3068, H5582, H1741): the LORD will prop him up on the couch of languishing -- saad, the bread-word of Psalm 104:15, food for a sick man. kol-mishkabo haphakhta be-cholyo (H4904, H2015, H2483): all his bed You TURN, the margin's literal -- the nurse's act of turning the mattress and the patient, or the turning of the sickness itself into health. God as the one at the bedside who does what a fevered man cannot.

4.text: As for me, I said, 'LORD, show me grace; heal my soul, because I have sinned against You.'
4.amp: I said [amar], LORD [YHWH], be merciful [chanan -- gracious] unto me: heal [rapha] my soul [nephesh]; for I have sinned [chet -- missed the mark] against You.
4.notes: ani-amarti YHWH chonneni (H559, H3068, H2603): 'I' -- the psalmist now the sick man of verses 1-3 -- said: be gracious; rephaah naphshi ki-chatati lakh (H7495, H5315, H2398): HEAL my soul, for I have sinned against You. He asks for healing on the ground of confession, not of merit: the illness and the sin are named in one breath, without saying which caused which (cf. Psalm 32:3-5; James 5:15-16).

5.text: My enemies speak evil about me: 'When will he die, and his name perish?'
5.amp: Mine enemies [oyeb] speak [amar] evil [ra] of me, When shall he die [muth], and his name [shem] perish [abad]?
5.notes: oyebai yomeru ra li (H341, H559, H7451): my enemies say evil 'to me' -- or about me -- matai yamut ve-abad shemo (H4191, H6, H8034): 'when will he die, and his name perish?' The sickroom visitors are counting down. For a king the question is dynastic: the name perishing means the line ending (cf. Psalm 9:5).

6.text: And when one comes to see me, he speaks empty words; his heart stores up malice for itself; then he goes out and talks.
6.amp: And if he come [bo] to see [raah] me, he speaks [dabar] vanity [shav -- emptiness]: his heart [leb] gathers [qabats] iniquity [aven] to itself; when he goes [yatsa] abroad [chuts -- outside], he tells [dabar] it.
6.notes: ve-im-ba lirot shav yedabber (H935, H7200, H7723, H1696): and if he comes to 'see' me -- the sick-visit -- he speaks shav, hollow comfort; libbo yiqbots-aven lo (H3820, H6908, H205): his heart COLLECTS wickedness for itself -- gathering material at the bedside -- yetse la-chuts yedabber (H3318, H2351, H1696): he goes outside and talks. The anatomy of a false friend in one verse: the visit is reconnaissance.

7.text: All who hate me whisper together against me; against me they plot my ruin:
7.amp: All that hate [sane] me whisper together [yachad] against me: against me do they devise [chashab] my hurt ['evil to me', ra, the KJV margin].
7.notes: yachad alai yitlachashu kol-soneai (H3162, H8130): together against me all my haters WHISPER -- the hissing verb, used of snake-charmers (Psalm 58:5); alai yachshebu raah li (H2803, H7451): against me they reckon 'evil to me', the margin's literal. Psalm 31:13's whispering, heard from a sickbed.

8.text: 'A deadly thing has been poured into him,' they say; 'now that he is down, he will never get up again.'
8.amp: An evil ['A thing of Belial', beliyyaal, the KJV margin] disease [dabar -- thing], say they, cleaves fast [yatsaq -- is poured out] unto him: and now that he lies [shakab] he shall rise up [qum] no more [yasaph].
8.notes: debar-beliyyaal yatsuq bo (H1697, H1100, H3332): 'a thing of Belial', the margin's literal -- a word of worthlessness, a deadly matter -- is POURED into him: yatsaq, cast like molten metal, fixed; va-asher shakhab lo-yosiph laqum (H7901, H3254, H6965): and he who has lain down will not add to rise. The visitors' verdict, and the psalm's turning point: verse 10 asks God for exactly the verb they denied.

9.text: Even the man I was at peace with, whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted his heel high against me.
9.amp: Yea, mine own familiar friend ['the man of my peace', ish shalom, the KJV margin], in whom I trusted [batach], which did eat [akal] of my bread [lechem], has lifted up ['magnified', gadal, the KJV margin] his heel [aqeb] against me.
9.notes: gam-ish shelomi asher-batachti bo (H376, H7965, H982): even 'the man of my peace', the margin's literal -- my covenant-friend -- in whom I trusted, okhel lachmi (H398, H3899): who ate my bread, higdil alai aqeb (H1431, H6119): has MAGNIFIED the heel against me -- the margin's verb: the kick of a horse, or the heel raised to tread. Ahithophel is the likely first referent (2 Samuel 15:12); Jesus quoted the line of Judas at the table (John 13:18), dropping 'in whom I trusted' -- He never had.

10.text: But You, O LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up, so that I may repay them.
10.amp: But You, O LORD [YHWH], be merciful [chanan -- gracious] unto me, and raise me up [qum], that I may requite [shalam -- repay] them.
10.notes: ve-attah YHWH chonneni va-haqimeni (H3068, H2603, H6965): 'but You' -- the pivot -- be gracious and RAISE me up: the qum the enemies said would never happen (v. 8); va-ashallemah lahem (H7999): and I will repay them -- in a king's mouth, the restoration of justice; the church has read the line, with verse 9, of the risen Christ, whose rising was the answer to the betrayer's meal.

11.text: By this I know that You delight in me: my enemy does not raise the victory shout over me.
11.amp: By this I know [yada] that You favour [chaphets -- delight in] me, because mine enemy [oyeb] does not triumph [rua -- raise the shout] over me.
11.notes: be-zot yadati ki-chaphatsta bi (H3045, H2654): by THIS I know You delight in me -- ki lo-yaria oyebi alai (H341, H7321): because my enemy does not RAISE THE SHOUT over me -- rua, the war-whoop of Jericho (Joshua 6:20), here the victory cry that never came. Survival read as a love-letter.

12.text: As for me, You hold me up in my integrity, and You set me before Your face forever.
12.amp: And as for me, You uphold [tamak] me in mine integrity [tom -- wholeness], and set [natsab -- station] me before Your face [panim] for ever [olam].
12.notes: va-ani be-tummi tamakhta bi (H8537, H8551): 'and I' -- in my integrity You have GRIPPED me; va-tatsibeni le-phanekha le-olam (H5324, H6440, H5769): and You STATION me before Your face forever -- natsab, the posture of a courtier who stands in the king's presence (cf. 1 Kings 17:1). The man the visitors wrote off is set on his feet in front of God, permanently.

13.text: Blessed be the LORD, Israel's God, from the everlasting past to the everlasting future! Amen, and Amen.
13.amp: Blessed [barak] be the LORD [YHWH] God [Elohim] of Israel [Yisrael] from everlasting [olam], and to everlasting [olam]. Amen [amen], and Amen [amen].
13.notes: barukh YHWH Elohe Yisrael me-ha-olam ve-ad ha-olam amen ve-amen (H1288, H3068, H430, H3478, H5769, H543): the doxology that closes Book One of the Psalter (Psalms 1-41) -- not part of David's sickbed prayer but the editors' seal, matched at 72:18-19, 89:52, 106:48. 'From the age to the age': the God who raised one sick king is blessed across all of them. Amen, and Amen: the congregation's double yes.
